clue.text: Knight's vehicle parked outside joint after wife dropped off

definitions.note: read as 'Knight is', the knight being the subject of the clue

indicators.note: something parked outside wraps around what follows, so the vehicle's letters go round the joint

parts.note: a tram is a street vehicle

indicators.note: dropped off says one letter is let go from the joint's word

parts.note: the wrist is a joint of the arm

explanation.surface: A knight's carriage waits outside a hostelry once his wife has been set down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joint' reads as a pub but is a body joint; 'dropped off' and 'parked outside' keep the vehicle surface going. Sir Tristram is a knight of the Round Table.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Tristram was one of King Arthur's knights of the Round Table, lover of Isolde.

clue.text: Strike the short Scouser's mate

indicators.note: short means cut off before the end, so the word the loses its final letter

parts.note: wack is Liverpool dialect for a friend; a Scouser is someone from Liverpool

explanation.surface: Hit the little Liverpudlian's friend.
explanation.walkthrough: A Scouser is a native of Liverpool, where WACK means mate or pal.
explanation.definitionFit: A thwack is a sharp heavy blow, so to thwack is to hit hard.

clue.text: Make drunk, mixing a beer in it

indicators.note: mixing means stirring together, so the letters of a beer in it are combined anew

explanation.surface: Getting someone drunk by stirring a beer into a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: To inebriate someone is to intoxicate them.

clue.text: Endure without protest what one may have to do with medicine when bedridden?

definitions.meaning: to accept a blow meekly, without fighting back

definitions.text: what one may have to do with medicine when bedridden?
definitions.meaning: a sick person in bed must swallow their dose while reclining

explanation.surface: A patient has to swallow medicine meekly while confined to bed.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means accepting ill treatment passively; literally it describes swallowing a dose while supine in bed.

clue.text: Fruit in a container, mostly loaded inside

indicators.note: inside places the shortened wealthy word within the container

parts.note: a pot is a container

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: loaded is slang for rich

explanation.surface: A fruit sits in a jar, which is nearly full inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loaded' reads as stuffed, matching the container picture, but is slang for wealthy; 'mostly' trims its last letter before 'inside' places it.
explanation.definitionFit: The apricot is a small orange stone fruit.

clue.text: A stubborn beast, last to exhibit charm

parts.note: the mule is proverbially stubborn

indicators.note: last to points at the final letter of the following word only

explanation.surface: A stubborn animal is the final creature to be shown off as charming.
explanation.definitionFit: An amulet is a charm worn to ward off evil, a talisman.

clue.text: Conventional place of refuge?

definitions.meaning: a traffic island in the centre of a street, where pedestrians shelter

explanation.surface: An ordinary sort of sanctuary.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means moderate or mainstream; literally the centre of a street is where pedestrian islands give shelter from traffic.

clue.text: Girl arranged loan to secure foremost of residences

indicators.note: to secure means to hold fast within, so the shuffled letters enclose the first letter
arranged means put in a new order, so the letters of loan are shuffled
foremost of takes the opening letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A young woman organised a mortgage to buy the best of the houses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' rearranges LOAN into LONA, and 'to secure' puts R inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Lorna is a girl's name, as in the novel Lorna Doone.

clue.text: Choose filling fare for the VIPs seated here?

indicators.note: filling means stuffed inside, so the choosing word goes into the fare word

parts.note: table means the food provided, as in keeping a good table
to opt is to choose

explanation.surface: Picking a satisfying meal for the important guests seated here.
explanation.walkthrough: 'filling fare' looks like a hearty meal; 'filling' is the insertion indicator and 'fare' is TABLE, food served.
explanation.definitionFit: The top table at a formal dinner is where the guests of honour sit.

clue.text: Disturbance caused by strange tailless cat

parts.note: rum is British slang for odd or strange

indicators.note: tailless means without its last letter, so the cat word is cut short

parts.note: puss is a cat

explanation.surface: Commotion caused by an odd cat without a tail.
explanation.walkthrough: RUM is old British slang for odd. The surface hints at a Manx, a tailless breed.
explanation.definitionFit: A rumpus is a noisy commotion or uproar.

clue.text: Crew adrift, large number from sunken vessel

indicators.note: adrift means drifting loose and out of place, so the letters of crew are scrambled

parts.note: K stands for a thousand, a large number

explanation.surface: Sailors drift away, many of them, from a ship that has gone down.
explanation.definitionFit: A wreck is the remains of a ship that has sunk or been destroyed.

clue.text: Set off after several drinks and journey there and back

indicators.note: after places the setting-off word behind the drinks word

parts.note: a round is a set of drinks bought for a group
to trip an alarm is to set it off

explanation.surface: Someone sets out after a few drinks on an out-and-back journey.
explanation.definitionFit: A round trip is a journey to a place and back again.

clue.text: Golf trophy is guarded by gruff copper heading for Pinehurst

indicators.note: something guarded by others is enclosed between them, so is sits between the gruff word and the copper symbol

parts.note: curt means brusque or gruff
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

indicators.note: heading for takes the initial letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A golf trophy is protected by a surly policeman on his way to Pinehurst, a famous US golf resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' looks like a policeman but is the chemical element. The Curtis Cup is a women's amateur golf match between Britain and Ireland and the USA.
explanation.definitionFit: The Curtis Cup is the trophy contested by women amateur golf teams from the USA and Great Britain and Ireland.

clue.text: Animal in a shaded avenue, set back

indicators.note: set back means moved backwards, so the whole phrase a shaded avenue is read in reverse

parts.note: a mall is a tree-lined walk, like The Mall in London

explanation.surface: A creature stands in a tree-shaded avenue, set back from the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set back' turns A MALL round as a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: The llama is a South American pack animal related to the camel.

clue.text: Wager involves everyone in Giselle?

indicators.note: involves means wraps up inside, so the wager word encloses the word for everyone

parts.note: a bet is a wager
all means everyone

explanation.surface: A bet that everyone joins in, placed on Giselle as though she were a racehorse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Giselle' reads as a woman or a horse; it is a classic ballet by Adolphe Adam, so the definition is by example, flagged by the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Giselle is a well-known Romantic ballet, an example of the dance form.

clue.text: Type of anorak, anorak ultimately carried by sad loners

indicators.note: something carried by others is held within them, so the final letter goes inside the rearranged loners
sad suggests something in a sorry state, so the letters of loners are jumbled
ultimately takes the closing letter of the repeated word

explanation.surface: A kind of anorak, and a nerdy anorak at that, is worn by lonely misfits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sad' rearranges LONERS into SNOREL, and 'carried by' puts K inside. In Britain an 'anorak' is also a slang name for an obsessive nerd, which the surface plays on.
explanation.definitionFit: A snorkel parka is a hooded winter jacket whose hood forms a tunnel, so it is a kind of hooded coat.

clue.text: Gull in pool reportedly weak, in distress

indicators.note: reportedly signals a word heard rather than spelt, so the pool word is written as it sounds

parts.note: a kitty is a shared pool of money

indicators.note: in distress means in a bad way, so the letters of weak are disturbed

explanation.surface: A seabird in a rock pool is said to be feeble and struggling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pool' looks like water but is a kitty of money, said aloud as KITTI.
explanation.definitionFit: The kittiwake is a small cliff-nesting gull named after its call.

clue.text: Fighter has to turn from the right course over channel

indicators.note: over in a down clue places the first word above the second

parts.note: to warp is to twist or bend from what is true or straight
a lane is a channel, as a shipping lane

explanation.surface: A fighter pilot has to veer off course across the English Channel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fighter' looks like a person; it is a fighter aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: A warplane is a military aircraft such as a fighter.

clue.text: A row involving the Spanish studio

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so the row word encloses the Spanish article

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: An argument breaks out involving Spanish people in an artist's workshop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' looks like a quarrel but is a tier of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: An atelier is an artist's or designer's workshop.

clue.text: Outcome in troubled Ulster

indicators.note: troubled means disturbed, so the letters of Ulster are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: The consequence of the Troubles in Northern Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: Ulster is Northern Ireland; 'troubled' nods to the Troubles there.
explanation.definitionFit: A result is the consequence or end product of something.

clue.text: Go round gallery after run out

indicators.note: after puts the gallery behind the run out letters

parts.note: ro is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for run out
the Tate is a group of London art galleries

explanation.surface: Someone tours an art gallery once they have been dismissed at cricket.
explanation.walkthrough: TATE is the famous London art gallery; RO is how a cricket scorecard records a batsman who is run out.
explanation.definitionFit: To rotate is to turn or revolve about an axis, to spin.

clue.text: Stock farm worker sprinted and caught that girl

parts.note: ran is the past tense of run, sprinted
c is the cricket abbreviation for caught
her refers to a female, that girl

explanation.surface: A cowhand dashed off and seized a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A rancher runs a ranch, a farm raising cattle or other livestock.

clue.text: Small piece of notepaper?

parts.note: a little sticky square for jotting reminders, or read as an instruction to send something by mail

explanation.definitionFit: A Post-it is a small adhesive note for reminders, and to post it is to mail it.

clue.text: Penny phoned causing crash

parts.note: rang means telephoned

explanation.surface: Penny made a call that led to an accident.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Penny' looks like a woman's name. PRANG is British slang for a minor car crash.
explanation.definitionFit: Prang is informal British slang for a minor smash-up, typically in a car or aircraft.

clue.text: Expect a delay

parts.note: a wait is a delay

explanation.surface: Anticipate a hold-up.
explanation.definitionFit: To await something is to wait for or anticipate it.

clue.text: Cruelly stab one in a garment worn by heretics

indicators.note: cruelly suggests harsh, twisting treatment, so the letters of stab one in are mangled

explanation.surface: Someone viciously stabs a victim dressed in the robe of a condemned heretic.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of STAB ONE IN gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The sanbenito was the yellow penitential robe the Spanish Inquisition made condemned heretics wear.

clue.text: Religious leader at a holy resort around LA

indicators.note: around means the rearranged letters sit on both sides of the city abbreviation
resort read as re-sort means sort again, so at a holy is rearranged

explanation.surface: A cleric visits a sacred holiday spot near Los Angeles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' looks like a holiday place but is read as re-sort, the anagram signal; 'around' then wraps the shuffled letters about Los Angeles.
explanation.definitionFit: An ayatollah is a senior Shiite Muslim cleric in Iran.

clue.text: Love some, but not all, abstract paintings

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, written as O
part means some but not the whole

explanation.surface: An art lover warms to a portion, though not the whole, of a show of abstract canvases.
explanation.definitionFit: Op art is a 1960s style of abstract painting using optical illusions.

clue.text: Straighten out former nurse

parts.note: ex means former
to tend is to nurse

explanation.surface: A one-time nurse sorts things out.
explanation.definitionFit: To extend a limb is to stretch it out straight.

clue.text: Incline to concede about stamp

indicators.note: about means going round, so the conceding word encloses the stamp

parts.note: to grant is to concede
a die is a tool that stamps a design

explanation.surface: Someone is inclined to give way over a postage stamp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Incline' reads as a verb but is the noun, a slope.
explanation.definitionFit: A gradient is the slope or steepness of a road or line.
